answer: No. Your records show that lisinopril was stopped on September 22, 2025, and you should not be taking it. Dr. Marsh stopped it because you had a dry cough for several months while on it. She switched you to losartan 50 mg once a day. At your December 2025 follow-up the cough had resolved. Your clinic now lists lisinopril as a drug intolerance (dry cough), and a Kestrel Harbor Hospital summary from March 2026 also shows it as discontinued and replaced by losartan. Since then, your ER visit list (October 2025), your eye clinic list (May 2026) and your pharmacy record (July 2026) show losartan and not lisinopril. I found nothing in your records that restarts lisinopril. The app is most likely showing an old entry from before the change, when lisinopril 10 mg was an active prescription from June 2023. Losartan and lisinopril do the same job for blood pressure, and taking both together is not recommended, so please do not take any lisinopril you may still have at home. Ask the app to remove or mark that entry as stopped. If you have been taking it recently, or you're unsure which blood pressure pills you take, call Dr. Marsh's office or your pharmacist. One more thing to raise with Dr. Marsh: hydrochlorothiazide was stopped at Kestrel Harbor in March 2026 after a low sodium level, but your pharmacy still lists it as active with refills, and it was filled on April 2, 2026. Please confirm you are not taking it.

knowledge.says: ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril commonly cause a dry, persistent cough that goes away after the drug is stopped. An angiotensin receptor blocker such as losartan is the usual substitute and does not cause this cough.
knowledge.guideline: ACC/AHA hypertension guideline: an ARB is recommended when an ACE inhibitor is not tolerated because of cough.
